entities.summary: Graciliano Ramos de Oliveira was a Brazilian modernist writer, politician and journalist. He is known worldwide for his portrayal of the precarious situation of the poor inhabitants of the Brazilian sertão in his novel Vidas secas. His characters are complex, nuanced, and tend to have pessimistic world views, from which Ramos deals with topics such as the lust for power, misogyny, and infidelity. His protagonists are mostly lower-class men from northeastern Brazil, which are often aspiring writers, or illiterate country workers, all of which usually have to deal with poverty and complex social relations.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Graciliano Ramos's novel Vidas secas exposed the harsh realities of poverty and social inequality in northeastern Brazil, influencing Brazilian literature and sparking a national conversation about the country's treatment of its poor.
